text: Lesson 2 walked two processes across several modules. Now let's slow down and look at the modules themselves — what each one actually covers, and what they share with each other.

Financials is the accounting core — GL, Payables, Receivables, Cash, Fixed Assets, Expenses. Procurement covers requisitions, purchase orders, and suppliers. Supply Chain covers inventory, order management, manufacturing, and planning. HCM covers people — core HR, compensation, payroll, and talent.

Modules integrate smoothly because they share master data — the same supplier record Procurement uses is the one Payables pays, the same customer record Order Management uses is the one Receivables bills, the same employee record approves a requisition or submits an expense report.

Three real examples: a purchase order in Procurement flows into a Payables invoice without retyping. Shipped inventory in Supply Chain automatically generates a cost-of-goods-sold entry in the General Ledger. An employee's expense report routes for approval using their HCM manager, then becomes a Financials reimbursement.

A support ticket rarely says the General Ledger is broken — it says an invoice won't post, and tracing that back means understanding the modules around Financials, not just Financials itself. Next up, Lesson 4: on-premises ERP versus cloud ERP.
